Anna and Sarah lived in
snowy Canada. They felt
much too hot for the
cold.

They were magical girls
made of glowing lava.
Snow melted into
puddles wherever they
stepped.

"We must go to
Malaysia," said Anna. "To
stop the villain Pedro
Pony!"

Sarah packed their bags
for a big adventure. They
flew high across the deep
blue sea.

They landed in beautiful,
sunny Malaysia. The
tropical heat felt just like
home.

"There is the villain!"
Sarah cried. They saw
Pedro Pony wearing a
scary mask.

But look! There are
cameras and bright
lights. Pedro Pony was
only acting in a movie.

"I am not a villain," Pedro
Pony said. "I just like
playing pretend on film!"

Adventure is better with
new friends. Malaysia is
the perfect place for lava
girls.

One bright little day, by the bay full of boats,
Sat Gus the Goat in his big blue coat.
He munched on his oats with a crunch and a chew,
And sang, ?This is lunch! This is lunch! This will do!?

Then Sam the Snake came down with a rake,
And cried, ?Oh no! Oh no! Where?s my cake?
I baked it last night by the soft moon light,
And I set it right here. It was round. It was white!?

Gus blinked once.
Then Gus blinked twice.
?I did not take your cake.
But it smelled rather nice.?

Sam hissed, ?You have jam on the tip of your chin!
And crumbs on your coat! And a grinny-goat grin!?
Gus said, ?That is oat-jam. I eat it with tea.
Your cake was not taken by goatish old me!?

Then up trotted Pip, with a cup and a map,
A red little hat and a blue little cap.
?What?s all this shouting by hill, lake, and tree?
A snake and a goat are too loud before tea!?

?My cake has been stolen!? said Sam with a shake.
?And Gus looks suspicious!?
?I did not!? bleated Gus.
?I ate oats, not cake!?

Pip looked at the mud.
Pip looked at the grass.
Pip looked through a round little looking-glass.
?There are marks by the path, and a print by the well.
And something smells sweet. I can follow that smell.?

So Gus and Sam followed Pip down the track,
Past a thin little twig and a thick muddy stack.
They passed a fish with a fin in a dish,
And a frog on a log making one birthday wish.

They passed a van by a very green vine,
A zebra with zip, and a pig-shaped sign.
They passed a small ship that whispered, ?Shh! Shh!
The cake went that way with a swish and a whoosh!?

They climbed up a hill to a strange little chair,
Where crumbs made a trail to a cave over there.
Inside sat a bear with a crown made of string,
A book, and a hook, and a bright silver ring.

The bear gave a cough.
The bear gave a sneeze.
Then cake flew out
From behind both his knees.

Sam shouted, ?My cake!?
Gus shouted, ?Aha!?
Pip shouted, ?Well, that is the weirdest thing?ha!?

The bear looked ashamed.
?My name is Ben Bear.
I found a lost cake by the lake over there.
I thought it said, ?Ben,? but it really said, ?Sam.?
And then I got cake on my knees and my jam.?

Sam looked at Ben.
Then he looked at the cake.
Then he looked at poor Gus, who was starting to shake.

?I blamed you too fast,? Sam said to the goat.
?I saw crumbs and jam and your big blue coat.
I should have asked Pip. I should have asked you.
A snake can be wrong. It is sadly quite true.?

Gus smiled and said, ?I forgive you, my friend.
But now that we?ve found it, how does this end??
Pip said, ?That?s easy. No shouting. No fight.
We slice it and share it before it turns night.?

So Sam cut the cake with a chop and a chat,
And Ben put a plate on the top of his hat.
Gus got a slice with a spoon and a tune,
And Pip got a piece shaped like half of the moon.

They ate by the fire.
They danced in the rain.
They rode down the hill on a very small train.
A cow on a cloud gave a laugh and a bow,
And the ship called, ?Hooray!? with a swish and a wow.

Now Gus by the bay always shares all his oats.
Sam labels his cakes with much bigger notes.
And Pip keeps a map in her red little pack,
In case any snack ever sneaks off the track.

So if cake disappears by the lake or the bay,
Do not hiss, do not bleat, do not shout right away.
Look under the chair. Look behind the bear?s knees.
Then share what you find and say,
?More cake, please!?

Anne had a red hat.
The red hat sat on Anne.
Anne ran to the gate.

"I am in my red hat," said Anne.
"I am glad in my red hat."

Diana ran to Anne.
Diana said, "I like the red hat."
Anne said, "I like it too."

Anne saw a sad cat.
The cat sat on a mat.
Anne sat by the cat.

"Are you sad?" Anne said.
The cat did not say.

Anne got a bit of milk.
The cat had the milk.
Now the cat was not sad.
Anne was glad.

Anne ran to the pond.
Diana ran to the pond.
The pond was still.

"I can see me," said Anne.
"I can see you," said Diana.

Anne put a hand in the pond.
The pond did not stay still.
"Oh!" said Anne.
"Now I can not see me!"

Anne sat in a big tree.
The tree was old.
The tree was tall.

"I like this old tree," said Anne.
"It is a good tree."

Marilla said, "Anne, get down."
Anne got down.
Then Anne said, "I still like that tree."

Matthew had a soft hat.
Anne had a lot to say.

Anne said, "I like red."
Anne said, "I like trees."
Anne said, "I like the sun."

Matthew did not say a lot.
Matthew just sat.
Then Matthew said, "I like that."
Anne said, "I like you, Matthew."

Robin had a red feather.
The red feather was soft.
Robin put it in his cap.

Little John saw the red feather.
?Can I see it?? said John.
?Yes,? said Robin.

John gave it back.
Robin gave a big grin.
The red feather was for both of them.

Robin had one bun.
The bun was warm.
The bun was good.

A small child came by.
The child had no bun.
Robin saw the child.

Robin cut the bun in two.
?Some for you,? said Robin.
?Some for me.?

Robin saw a little goat.
The goat was by a log.
The goat said, ?Maa.?

?Are you lost?? said Robin.
The goat went maa, maa.
Robin went tap, tap.

The goat ran to the gate.
The goat was home.
Robin was glad.

Rain fell in the wood.
Tap, tap, tap.
Robin ran to a tree.

Marian ran to the tree too.
?Rain, rain,? said Marian.
?Tap, tap,? said Robin.

The rain went away.
The sun came out.
Robin and Marian ran home.

Robin had a green hat.
The hat sat on Robin.
The wind went whoosh.

The hat went up.
The hat went down.
The hat sat on a bush.

Robin got the hat.
?Good hat,? said Robin.
The hat sat on Robin again.

Pippa sees a little frog.
It sits and sits upon a log.
"Come play with me," says Pippa Pig.
The frog says nothing. That is big.

"Let's jump and splash," says Pippa Pig.
The frog just stares. He is a fog.
"Can you not talk?" says Pippa Pig.
The frog sits still upon his log.

Then Georgie hops up and gives a shove.
The frog flies off -- oh, dear, oh, love!
"Where did he go?" Pippa says, "Oh, my!"
Then Mama Pig says, "That's a fly."
The frog was a toy all along.
Pippa laughs, "I sang the wrong song!"
